nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of CoWO3 on carbon cloth

nodes.name: Pt loading and NH3 annealing on CoWO3
nodes.procedure: Co-doped WO3 (noted as CoWO3) grown on carbon cloth was first prepared by a hydrothermal method, and then immersed in H2PtCl6 solution, followed by a thermal annealing treatment in an NH3 atmosphere to form Pt/N-CoWO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples display diffraction peaks of hexagonal WO3 (JCPDF No. 85-2460) and metallic Pt (JCPDF No. 04-0802). No diffraction peaks corresponding to Co nanoparticles on Pt/N-CoWO3 and Pt/CoWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns in Figure 1b show that all the samples display the diffraction peaks of hexagonal WO3 (JCPDF No. 85-2460) and metallic Pt (JCPDF No. 04-0802).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/N-CoWO3 shows rough nanorods structure, different from nanowire structure of Pt/N-WO3 without Co addition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image of Pt/N-CoWO3 shows the rough nanorods structure (Figure 1c), different from the nanowire structure of Pt/N-WO3...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images of Pt/N-CoWO3 exhibit lattice spacing of 0.320 nm and 0.225 nm attributing to (020) plane of WO3 and (111) plane of Pt, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of Pt/N-CoWO3 (Figure 1d-e) exhibit the lattice spacing of 0.320 and 0.225 nm attributing to the (020) plane of WO3 and (111) plane of Pt...

nodes.characterization_summary: Amounts of Pt and Co determined to be 1.25 and 0.28 wt.% respectively for Pt/N-CoWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amounts of Pt and Co are determined to be 1.25 and 0.28 wt.% by inductively coupled plasmas mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), respectively (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows diffraction patterns indexed to (002), (200), (202), (220), and (222) planes of WO3 and (111) plane of Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern shows the diffraction patterns indexed to the (002), (200), (202), (220), and (222) planes of WO3 and (111) plane of Pt (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping images verify homogeneous distribution of W, Co, O, Pt, and N elements in Pt/N-CoWO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images verify a homogeneous distribution of W, Co, O, Pt, and N elements in the Pt/N-CoWO3 (Figure 1g)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f spectrum of Pt/N-CoWO3 shows dominant Pt⁰ peaks at 71.3 eV and 74.7 eV, Ptδ+ at 71.9 and 75.4 eV. W 4f shows W⁶+ at 35.9 and 38.0 eV, W⁵+ at 35.1 and 37.2 eV with 22.17% W⁵+ (higher than 14.14% in Pt/N-WO3). N 1s shows peaks at 402.4 eV (quaternary), 400.4 eV (pyrrolic), 398.4 eV (pyridinic N), 398.5 eV (Pt-N bonds, 3.11% higher than 2.19% in Pt/N-WO3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f spectrum of Pt/N-CoWO3 is divided into two peaks of Pt 4f5/2 and Pt 4f7/2 (Figure S5a)... The dominant peaks of the Pt 4f spectrum at 71.3 eV and 74.7 eV are attributed to the existence of Pt⁰, while the peaks at 71.9 and 75.4 eV are ascribed to Ptδ+.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₂-edge XANES of Pt/N-CoWO3 shows energy absorption threshold between Pt foil and PtO₂, higher white line intensity than Pt/N-WO3 indicating higher Pt oxidation state. W L₃-edge close to WO3 phase. Co K-edge between Co foil and CoO indicating Coδ+ (0<δ<2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a displays the Pt L₂-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of the Pt/N-WO3 and Pt/N-CoWO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₂-edge EXAFS shows Pt-N/O peak below 2 Å, stronger in Pt/N-CoWO3 than Pt/N-WO3. Pt-Pt bond at 2.36 Å in Pt/N-CoWO3. Coordination numbers: Pt-N/O 4.0, Pt-Pt 3.1. W L₃-edge first peak at 1.3 Å (W-O) increases to 1.37 Å after Co doping. Co K-edge shows Co-N/O at 1.5 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination environment has been probed by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) results.

properties.description: Fourier Transform of Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure spectrum

nodes.characterization_summary: Rietveld refinements show three phases in Pt/N-CoWO3: WO3 (93.1%), Pt₇.₂₇W₂₄O₁₈₀ (6.6%), and metallic Pt. Full-range synchrotron PDF analysis confirms Pt/Co at 6g and N at 6f Wyckoff positions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic pair distribution function (PDF) measurements were implemented to reveal the interatomic distances and the local structure of Pt/N-CoWO3 in real space.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/N-CoWO3 shows smallest charge transfer resistance of 2.373 Ω.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) presents that Pt/N-CoWO3 has the smallest charge transfer resistance of 2.373 Ω...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/N-CoWO3 possesses double-layer capacitance Cdl of 277.67 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt/N-CoWO3 possesses a larger Cdl of 277.67 mF cm⁻² than the Pt/WO3 (191.10 mF cm⁻²)...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of Pt/N-CoWO3 shows bands at ≈699, ≈808, ≈949 cm⁻¹ (O-W-O stretching), ≈320, ≈245 cm⁻¹ (W=O deformation). O-W-O peak shifts to higher wavenumber (≈808 cm⁻¹) after Co doping. Peak intensity decreases with cathodic potential due to proton insertion/extraction. New peak at 2352 cm⁻¹ (Pt-H) appears at -0.1 V vs Ag/AgCl.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further probe the catalytic mechanism of Pt/N-CoWO3, in situ Raman spectroscopy was conducted for the catalysts.
